chapter.title: Lesser-Known Built-in Hooks
chapter.description: Three hooks that solve specific problems custom hooks often need.

blocks.text: Accessible markup needs ids that link labels to inputs. `useId` generates one that matches between the server render and the client, which `Math.random()` cannot do.
`useId` is for accessibility attributes, not for list keys. Keys must come from your data, and `useId` returns the same value on every render of the same component instance.

blocks.caption: React DevTools shows the label next to the hook. It has no effect in production.

blocks.text: When a value lives outside React - a browser API, a third-party store, an event emitter - this hook subscribes to it safely, including during concurrent rendering.
This is the hook state libraries use internally. You rarely call it directly, but knowing it exists explains how Zustand and Redux stay consistent with concurrent React.

blocks.title: Write a debounce helper
blocks.instructions: Complete debounce so the returned function only calls fn after the given delay, restarting the timer on each call.

tests.name: It does not call immediately
tests.code: var n = 0; var f = debounce(function () { n++; }, 50); f(); return n === 0;

tests.name: Repeated calls restart the timer
tests.code: var n = 0; var f = debounce(function () { n++; }, 50); f(); f(); f(); return n === 0;
